doc: According to the Johns Hopkins University COVID-19 dashboard, as of October 23, 2020, the U.S. had recorded 3,353,056 recoveries out of 8,406,718 cases, yielding a case recovery rate of 39.88%. Globally, there were 28,349,541 recoveries out of 41,705,699 cases, a recovery rate of 67.97%. In the U.S., 223,042 deaths were reported out of 8,406,718 cases as of October 23, equivalent to a case fatality rate of 2.65%. The global case fatality rate stood at 2.72%.
label: False

normalized_claim: India’s imports from China increased by 27% in April-August 2020
claim: India’s imports from China increased by 27% in April-August 2020
doc: India's imports from China did not increase between April and August 2020; they actually decreased. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal confirmed that India's imports from China declined by 27.63 per cent during April–August 2020-21 over the corresponding period of the previous year.
label: False

normalized_claim: India's imports from China increased by 27% during the period April-August 2020.
claim: India's imports from China increased by 27% during the period April-August 2020.
doc: India's imports from China declined sharply in 2020. From January to February 2020, India's imports from China were as low as US$9.5 billion, reflecting a 12.4 per cent trade decline in the initial two months of COVID-19. Imports fell to a record low of USD 3.2 billion in both April and May 2020, coinciding with pandemic-induced lockdowns, before recovering to USD 4.8 billion in June and USD 5.6 billion in July—nearly back to the pre-lockdown level of USD 5.8 billion in March. For the first seven months of 2020, India's imports from China totalled USD 32.2 billion, still down 24.7% year-on-year. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal confirmed that imports from China declined by 27.63% during April–August 2020.
label: False
perturb_type2_False: India's imports from China increased by -27% during the period April-August 2020.

normalized_claim: 30% to 40% of Americans will have voted by Oct. 1. 2020
claim: 30% to 40% of Americans will have voted by Oct. 1. 2020
doc: In the 2016 U.S. presidential election, more than 41% of all ballots were cast before Election Day. By early October 2020, 3.3 million people had already voted, compared to only 74,836 at a similar point before the 2016 election. University of Florida professor Michael McDonald estimated total 2020 general election turnout at 150 million voters, meaning approximately 2.2% of the electorate had voted by early October. In reality, approximately 240 million people were eligible to vote in 2020 and roughly 66.1% submitted ballots, totalling about 158 million.
label: False
perturb_type2_False: -30% to 40% of Americans will have voted by Oct. 1. 2020

claim: Economic damage caused by the pandemic shows United States GDP (gross domestic product) falling by 33 percent compared to India's 23.9 percent drop.
doc: The United States and India report GDP growth and contraction differently. The U.S. GDP dropped by 9.1% during April to June 2020 on an annualised basis, while India's GDP contracted by 23.9%. When compared using the same reporting methodology, the U.S. GDP contraction during April to June 2020 was 9.1%.
